title: A Parish for the Cipher
premise: Freya Kavanagh, a night-shift taxi dispatcher with a gift for reading patterns in other people's emergencies, is pulled into a new case when a murder victim is found wearing clothes taken from her own closet. The dead man was the last known contact of Tomas Bell, a witness to a fatal fire twenty years ago whom the town of Ashmoor insists died in that fire — yet someone keeps sending Freya coded dispatch calls that only Tomas could compose. As she follows the cipher through the parish's archives, graveyards, and the taxi company's own ledgers, Freya uncovers a conspiracy of respectable families who staged the fire to erase Tomas's testimony about their patriarch's crimes. The trail ends in the flooded crypt beneath St. Alder's parish, where Freya finds Tomas alive, hidden for two decades by the one conspirator whose conscience outlasted the rest, and must choose between exposing the truth — which will destroy the belonging she has finally found in Ashmoor — or letting the parish keep its buried memory.
about_author: E. M. Ishikawa is a former emergency-services dispatcher turned novelist who writes mysteries steeped in small-town memory and moral fog. Known for meticulous plotting and quiet, haunted prose, Ishikawa lives in a coastal town that inspires the fictional parishes of the Freya Kavanagh series.

chapters.title: The Quiet Hours
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A slow night shift establishes her world: the dispatch board, her habit of noticing what callers don't say, and the three 'accidents' she quietly unraveled. When a call comes in about a body behind St. Alder's, her routine shatters. Emotional beat: the comfort of invisibility about to be stripped away.

chapters.title: Wrong Clothes for a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the scene, she recognizes her own gray coat and scarf on the corpse — items stolen from her flat. Detective Inspector Sorrell, who owes her for past cases, lets her look closer. Emotional beat: violation and vertigo; the case is suddenly personal.

chapters.title: A Name the Town Forbids
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The victim is identified as a records clerk who recently requested the Ashmoor parish fire file of 2004. Every mention of the sole witness, Tomas Bell, has been struck through with 'deceased.' Emotional beat: the first pull of an old wound the town wants closed.

chapters.title: Dispatch, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Back on shift, a garbled radio call arrives using an obsolete dispatch code — one only someone inside the old system would know. The phrasing echoes Tomas Bell's handwriting in archived logs. Emotional beat: a chill of being spoken to across time.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Burned
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, with a 2004 flashback interlude. She reconstructs the parish fire that killed the elder Alderton and supposedly Tomas Bell; no body was ever confirmed. Emotional beat: grief for a boy the town buried twice.

chapters.title: Sorrell's Warning
chapters.summary: Alternating Freya and Sorrell POVs. Sorrell admits the fire file was flagged by someone 'above his head' and begs her to drop it. Freya refuses. Emotional beat: alliance strained by fear; trust offered anyway.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Ledgers
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She discovers the dead clerk had annotated taxi company ledgers with a substitution cipher keyed to dispatch codes. The first decoded line: 'HE IS NOT ASH.' Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt returning, sharper now.

chapters.title: Mrs. Okafor Remembers
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. An elderly parishioner recalls Tomas as a choirboy who hid in the crypt during the fire — and mentions the Alderton family's charity that bought the town's silence. Emotional beat: warmth of community shadowed by complicity.

chapters.title: Second Message
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A second coded call routes a taxi to the flooded quarry at 3 a.m.; she goes and finds the clerk's missing notebook, half waterlogged. Someone watches from the treeline. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Family That Gave
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She maps the Alderton heirs — a judge, a developer, a vicar — and the web of endowments holding Ashmoor together. Exposing the truth could bankrupt the parish. Emotional beat: the cost of truth made visible.

chapters.title: What the Closet Knew
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Forensics show the stolen clothes were taken weeks ago, meaning someone had access to her home long before the murder. She finds a displaced floorboard and a hidden key. Emotional beat: paranoia blooming in her own rooms.

chapters.title: The Key of St. Alder's
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The key fits the parish's crypt gate, locked since the fire. The vicar, Daniel Alderton, catches her there and, surprisingly, hands her the fire's true blueprint. Emotional beat: an unexpected ally inside the guilty family.

chapters.title: Decoded Confession
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The notebook cipher yields a partial confession: the fire was arson to silence Tomas, who saw the elder Alderton kill a land protester. The clerk was killed for finding this. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Night Caller
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A third coded call comes from inside her own building. She traps the watcher: a frightened teenage boy, Rowan, who claims a 'kind uncle' pays him to deliver messages — and that the uncle lives in the crypt. Emotional beat: the mystery gains a living pulse.

chapters.title: The Judge's Ledger
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She breaks into Judge Alderton's chambers and finds payments spanning twenty years — hush money to the taxi company's old owner. Her own employer has been a cog in the cover-up. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution that raised her.

chapters.title: Sorrell Under Pressure
chapters.summary: Sorrell's POV. He is ordered to suspend Freya as a 'person of interest' in the clerk's murder. He stalls, passing her the case file through the back door. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against career and law.

chapters.title: The Quarry at Low Water
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Drought lowers the quarry; she finds the clerk's car and evidence the 'uncle' uses it. Fresh footprints lead toward the parish. Emotional beat: the hidden world drawing nearer.

chapters.title: Rowan's Uncle
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Rowan describes the uncle: a scarred, soft-spoken man who never shows his face, leaves food money, and asks only that messages be sent 'to the girl who listens.' Freya realizes she was chosen long ago. Emotional beat: being seen after years of hiding.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Marcus Alderton offers her money and a quiet relocation to stop digging, revealing they know about her three solved 'accidents.' She declines. Emotional beat: temptation refused; the point of no return crossed.

chapters.title: Fire, Again
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The parish archive burns overnight. The 2004 originals she needed are ash — but she had photographed the cipher pages. The arsonist's accelerant matches the old fire exactly. Emotional beat: history repeating, and her refusal to let it.

chapters.title: What Sorrell Kept
chapters.summary: Sorrell's POV. He confesses that in 2004, as a young constable, he falsified the death certificate under orders — Tomas Bell was never confirmed dead. His guilt has been the cipher's first key all along. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into courage.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Listens
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Decoding the final messages, she finds a meeting request: St. Alder's crypt, the anniversary eve of the fire, midnight. The handwriting is unmistakably an adult Tomas Bell's. Emotional beat: hope and dread in equal measure.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The town holds its memorial service above while she slips below. The crypt's flood channels have kept a hidden chamber dry for twenty years. Emotional beat: descending into the town's buried heart.

chapters.title: The Man in the Crypt
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She meets Tomas Bell: scarred, half-feral, sustained by the one conspirator who fed him — the late Mrs. Alderton, who repented and left him the crypt key. He has been sending the ciphers to test whether anyone could be trusted. Emotional beat: the witness found; the story's ground shifts.

chapters.title: His Twenty Years
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He recounts the fire, his escape into the crypt, the slow bargain of silence and bread, and why he chose Freya: her dispatch logs showed a mind that heard the unheard. Emotional beat: loneliness answered at last.

chapters.title: The Vicar's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Daniel Alderton's POV. Torn between family and faith, he has secretly shielded Tomas's trail. His brother the judge suspects. Emotional beat: conscience at war with blood.

chapters.title: The Judge Moves
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Judge Alderton, learning Tomas lives, moves to finish what 2004 started: he has Rowan taken to force the crypt's location. Emotional beat: the stakes turn intimate and lethal.

chapters.title: Missing Boy
chapters.summary: Freya and Sorrell POVs. Rowan's disappearance galvanizes the town; Mrs. Okafor's quiet testimony finally finds ears. Freya must trade Tomas's safety for the boy's. Emotional beat: the community waking from its long complicity.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She offers the judge the cipher notebook in exchange for Rowan, secretly having copied every page. The handoff at the quarry goes wrong when the developer brings a gun. Emotional beat: a trap sprung from both sides.

chapters.title: Quarry Edge
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the standoff, Marcus Alderton panics; the judge coldly calculates. Sorrell arrives with warrants and a constable's old courage. Rowan is saved; the notebook changes hands. Emotional beat: chaos survived, but the true villain still standing.

chapters.title: The Judge's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Confronted with the full decoded confession and Tomas alive, the judge invokes privilege and family — until the vicar, his own brother, testifies. Emotional beat: the empire of silence cracking from within.

chapters.title: Above Ground
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas walks into daylight for the first time in twenty years, into a churchyard full of neighbors who once sang beside him. Emotional beat: terror and grace of being known.

chapters.title: What the Town Owes
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Arrests ripple through Ashmoor; the taxi company's owner is implicated; Freya is suspended, then quietly vindicated. Some neighbors thank her; some never will. Emotional beat: belonging that must survive being costly.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Grave
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The murdered records clerk is buried with honors; Freya finishes his cipher and finds his last entry was a plea to give Tomas his name back. Emotional beat: mourning turned to completion.

chapters.title: Sorrell's Case
chapters.summary: Sorrell's POV. He formally reopens the 2004 fire as homicide, with Freya as consultant — on the record this time. Emotional beat: the invisible made official; partnership cemented.

chapters.title: The Parish Decides
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The parish votes on whether to demolish or memorialize the crypt. Mrs. Okafor's speech tips it: memory kept, not buried. Emotional beat: a community choosing its better self.

chapters.title: Freya's Choice
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The Alderton estate's collapse offers her hush money one last time through an intermediary. She burns the check on St. Alder's step. Emotional beat: the theme of inheritance answered — she inherits the truth instead.

chapters.title: A Name Restored
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A new headstone is carved for Tomas Bell — and he is alive to read it, laughing. He takes a job in the dispatch office, learning to listen as she does. Emotional beat: resurrection in the ordinary sense.

chapters.title: The Cipher Closes
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Climax's aftermath: the final cipher message, unsent until now, is Tomas's thank-you — and a warning that the clerk's files referenced one more unaccounted conspirator, still at large. Emotional beat: peace edged with vigilance.

chapters.title: A Parish for the Cipher
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A year later: night shift, familiar rhythms, Rowan apprenticing at the radio, Tomas two desks away. A coded call comes in from a stranger who 'heard she listens.' Freya smiles and answers. Emotional beat: belonging found — and the next mystery beginning.
